items.q: Were people executed in the witch craze because their magic really worked?
items.correct: No — accusations were driven by fear, religious upheaval, scapegoating and misogyny.
items.misconception: Yes, they had real magical powers.
items.why: Belief in the Devil and social tension drove accusations, mostly against women.

items.q: Did witch trials happen evenly everywhere and at all times?
items.correct: No — they peaked in particular periods and places, linked to instability.
items.misconception: Yes, evenly across all of history.
items.random_wrong: There were no witch trials in Europe.
items.why: Religious conflict and crises help explain when and where trials clustered.

items.q: Were only old women accused of witchcraft?
items.correct: Most accused were women, but men and people of many ages were too.
items.why: Vulnerable and marginalised people were especially at risk of accusation.
